Faint CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2, and S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, difficult to resolve in early frames but becoming more defined as it travels into the field-of-view. This front may be related to a slow, faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-05-28T01:57Z centered around S33E28 south of AR 14436 (S16E29). Though early, that source could also relate to later CME/streamer blowout 2026-05-28T09:23Z.

data.note: Faint CME visible well to the E in STEREO A COR, and as a faint partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 comprised of multiple overlapping features, clearly a complex structure. This front may be related to a slow, faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-05-28T01:57Z centered around S33E28 south of AR 14436 (S16E29), which is more directly attributed to earlier CME: 2026-05-28T03:38Z but this front at T9:23Z resembles more of streamer blowout and could simply be outflow following from that first signature. No distinct eruptive activity is seen relating to this start time.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-05-28T19:53Z, and this event is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an eruption near Active Region 14455 (N18E63) starting around 2026-05-28T19:30Z which exhibits northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/195/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME, however prolonged moving/opening field lines are visible beyond the W limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-05-28T21:00Z which may be more associated with the northern lobe of this feature.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning around 2026-05-29T17:03Z. Some of the early propagation of this CME is missed in running difference imagery due to poor image quality. This CME is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a small eruption centered around S24W58 best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-05-29T16:06Z as some ejecta with significant westward deflection. There is an additional feature in STEREO A COR2 around the same time, but this is most likely related to a far-sided, different source.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-05-29T17:09Z. This CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely some ejecta seen from beyond the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 around 2026-05-29T16:45Z. There is a similar feature in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 (CME: 2026-05-29T17:03Z) which was determined to be from a front-sided, separate source.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 beginning around 2026-05-29T18:00Z. It is also seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 but is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a failed filament eruption centered around N65W00. The filament can be seen lifting off and mostly falling back beginning around 2026-05-29T16:00Z in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as visible source location.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-05-29T20:24Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely field line movement beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-05-29T19:43Z. The CME mostly dissipates before reaching the FOV of SOHO LASCO C3.

data.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a small eruption centered near S10E15 starting around 2026-05-30T00:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/193/304, STEREO A EUVI 304, and GOES SUVI 131/195/284/304 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption centered near N25E65 which begins to lift off around 2026-05-29T23:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb around this time in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible as a northwest partial halo in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and a northeast halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Although no evidence of an eruption was visible on the Earth-facing disk, the Solar Orbiter STIX instrument, which was located at longitude -155 at the time of this event, observed the equivalent of a ~C9 flare peaking at 2026-05-30T08:01Z. Additionally, STEREO Ahead observed an increase in the 13-100 MeV protons starting around 2026-05-30T09:00Z, with a peak value of 0.02 pfu/MeV observed at 2026-05-30T10:15Z. It is possible the source is related to former Active Region 14436, located at N18E150 at the time of this event, based on prior activity from this region when it was on the Earth-facing disk. Additionally, the triangulated CME measurement places the CME in the vicinity of former Active Region 14436.

The source is likely a prominence over the SW limb observed first in STEREO A EUVI 304 as early as 2026-05-30T15:15Z, and in SDO AIA 171 as field line movement starting around 2026-05-30T17:00Z.
